xBRIEFInfo.description: Plan for PAN-2702: Strike agents should land on main without requiring the Flywheel — deacon-owned strike merge handoff

plan.title: Strike agents should land on main without requiring the Flywheel — deacon-owned strike merge handoff
plan.author: agent:gpt-5.6-sol

narratives.Problem: Strike agents finish with a pushed, verified strike branch but signal readiness only to the optional Flywheel session, so finished emergency fixes can remain unmerged for hours when Flywheel is absent.
narratives.Proposal: Persist a strike-ready remote HEAD through the canonical pipeline writer, have Deacon claim it and invoke the existing server merge door with explicit strike context, and re-drive the warm strike agent on actionable conflicts or gate failures for up to three fresh-HEAD cycles before needs-you escalation.
narratives.NonGoals:
- Do not change the normal review → test → UAT → human/auto-merge lane or its eligibility rules.
- Do not exempt `agent-*` or `strike-*` identities from the main-push guard.
- Do not create a second merge implementation, direct local-main push path, or separate task/state store.
- Do not make Flywheel required for strike landing or assign it sole ownership of the marker.
- Do not change repository-wide forge merge method/history policy.
- Do not restart the live dashboard server during implementation verification.

autoDecisions.summary: Use a dedicated `pan strike-ready <id>` signal instead of overloading `pan done --strike` or parsing readiness text.
autoDecisions.rationale: The existing `--strike` form means post-merge completion, while a dedicated command can validate branch identity and persist an unambiguous machine-readable event.

autoDecisions.summary: Use three self-recovery cycles and require a new remote strike HEAD for each retry.
autoDecisions.rationale: Three matches the issue's suggested bounded range and prevents repeated patrols from consuming budget without new agent work.

autoDecisions.summary: Reuse triggerMerge and its forge merge semantics rather than changing the global merge method.
autoDecisions.rationale: The requirement prioritizes the existing verified merge door and revertibility; changing normal history policy would exceed the strike-lane scope.

items.title: Persist an authenticated strike-ready signal

expected_outputs: strike-ready command and durable round-trip tests pass

narrative.Action: Add `pan strike-ready <issueId>` as the only strike completion signal. The command must resolve the configured project, require the current workspace/registered worktree to be `workspaces/feature-<issue>-strike` on `strike/<issue>`, fetch `origin/strike/<issue>`, require the local committed HEAD to equal the pushed remote HEAD, and write the marker through `setReviewStatusSync` (never direct DB/state access). Extend ReviewStatus, SQLite schema/migrations and sync mapping, durable status subset, PanIssuePipelineRecord, and record projection with: signaled remote HEAD, ready timestamp, landing state (`ready|landing|recovering|landed|needs_you`), recovery cycle count, and structured attempt history containing timestamp, strike HEAD, main HEAD, outcome, and detail. A new signal for a new HEAD resets landing state to ready but preserves prior attempt history; an identical HEAD signal is idempotent and must not consume recovery budget. Update `src/cli/commands/strike.ts` prompt and `roles/strike.md` to invoke this command after gates/push and remove Flywheel tell/comment fallback. Do not modify the main-push guard.

items.title: Given a committed strike branch whose local and remote HEADs match, `pan strike-ready PAN-2702` persists that HEAD and produces landing state `ready` through the canonical writer.
Given a non-strike workspace, wrong branch, dirty/unpushed commit, or mismatched remote HEAD, the command rejects the signal and preserves the prior durable marker.
Given the same pushed HEAD is signaled twice, the writer preserves one readiness cycle and does not increment recovery count or duplicate attempt history.
A cache rebuild from the issue record restores the strike readiness HEAD, landing state, recovery count, and attempt history without loss.
Route strike branches through the canonical merge door

expected_outputs: strike merge-door and normal eligibility regression tests pass

narrative.Action: Refactor `triggerMerge(issueId)` to accept an optional discriminated strike request carrying the marker HEAD, strike workspace, `strike/<issue>` branch, and `strike-<issue>` recovery target. The normal/default call must retain every existing review/test/UAT/readyForMerge check. The strike call is eligible only when the durable landing state is `ready`, the recorded HEAD still equals `origin/strike/<issue>`, and the workspace/branch identity matches. Reuse the persistent per-project merge queue, `_serverManagedMerges`, PR creation, post-rebase quality gates, forge adapter merge, and `postMergeLifecycle(issueId, projectPath, branchName)`; do not add a local main push or bypass verification. Parameterize the current work-agent rebase handoff so the strike lane addresses the warm strike session and instructs it to re-signal after pushing. Preserve the existing forge merge method. Add a focused no-loss matrix proving all pre-existing normal triggerMerge gates and outcomes remain unchanged.

items.title: Given a valid durable strike marker, the merge door resolves `feature-<issue>-strike` and `strike/<issue>`, runs the configured post-rebase gates, merges through the forge adapter, and invokes postMergeLifecycle with the strike branch.
Given the marker HEAD differs from `origin/strike/<issue>`, the strike merge request rejects before PR creation, verification, or merge and records the concrete stale-signal reason.
Given a normal pipeline call, every prior review, test, UAT, queue, and already-merging eligibility outcome is preserved by the no-loss audit test.
The main-push guard rejects direct `main` pushes from both agent and strike identities after the merge-door refactor.
Consume ready strikes from the Deacon patrol

expected_outputs: Deacon strike landing and patrol ordering tests pass

narrative.Action: Add a focused Deacon patrol helper that reads strike markers through the canonical review-status resolver, skips ignored/stuck/terminal/non-ready entries, atomically changes the matching HEAD from `ready` to `landing` through the writer before external work, and invokes the strike form of `triggerMerge`. Wire it into `runPatrol()` once per configured patrol interval. Treat a queued/in-progress/already-merged result as an idempotent observation, and mark successful completion `landed` without starting a second lifecycle. A Flywheel caller that observes the same marker must converge through the shared merge queue/landing state rather than double-merge. Use injected dependencies in unit tests and fake timers for cadence behavior.

items.title: Given Flywheel is absent and a strike marker is ready, the next Deacon patrol claims it and invokes the canonical strike merge door.
Given two observers race on the same signaled HEAD, exactly one claim starts merge work and the other observes landing, queued, or terminal state without issuing a second merge.
Given a successful merge result, the patrol persists landing state `landed`, clears readiness, and produces one action message naming the issue and merged strike HEAD.
Re-drive actionable strike landing failures

expected_outputs: bounded strike recovery and needs-you tests pass using fake timers

narrative.Action: Classify strike merge failures into agent-actionable (main moved, rebase conflict, stale marker, drifted anchors, branch/CI or configured gate failure) and non-actionable (merge guard refusal, missing project/integration permission, unavailable infrastructure). For an actionable failure below the three-cycle budget, append an attempt containing old strike HEAD, current main SHA, conflict files or failed check output, transition to `recovering`, and deliver a complete recovery request to `strike-<issue>` using async message delivery/resurrection without overriding an operator pause. The request must tell the strike to fetch/rebase current main, resolve, rerun configured gates, push only `strike/<issue>`, and run `pan strike-ready <issue>` again. Do not retry until a fresh remote HEAD signal arrives. For a non-actionable failure, failed delivery, or exhausted third cycle, persist `needs_you`, write feedback, and call the existing needs-you/stuck surface once with the full ordered attempt history.

items.title: Given main moved and the strike branch conflicts, the patrol appends the conflict files and new main SHA, delivers them to `strike-<issue>`, and produces landing state `recovering` without emitting needs-you.
Given the strike pushes and signals a fresh HEAD after recovery, the next patrol accepts the new cycle and can produce landing state `landed` without operator involvement.
Given the same HEAD is re-signaled or no fresh signal arrives, later patrols preserve the recovery count and do not rerun merge work or resend recovery feedback.

Given three actionable cycles fail, or a non-actionable failure occurs, the system emits needs-you exactly once and includes every attempted HEAD, main SHA, failed check/conflict, and delivery outcome.
Document Deacon-owned strike landing

expected_outputs: prompt and skill lint complete without errors

narrative.Action: Update `docs/QUICK-REFERENCE.md` and the strike/merge sections of `docs/SPECIALIST_WORKFLOW.md` to define the full operator-visible lane: the strike pushes only its strike branch, `pan strike-ready` durably hands ownership to Deacon, Deacon uses the existing verified merge queue without Flywheel, actionable failures return to the warm strike session for three fresh-HEAD cycles, and needs-you is the terminal escalation with attempt history. Ensure `pan --help`/command description and `roles/strike.md` use the same terminology and remove claims that the spawner/Flywheel must land the branch.

items.title: The quick reference produces a `pan strike-ready <id>` entry that states Deacon lands the pushed strike branch through the verified merge door without Flywheel.
The specialist workflow produces a recovery section that describes three fresh-HEAD cycles and states that needs-you includes ordered failure history after recovery is exhausted or impossible.
